candidate.design_rationale: The report identifies a randomized, double-blind, parallel-group trial; patients were individually assigned 1:1 to empagliflozin or placebo.
candidate.target_measurement: Time to first adjudicated event of cardiovascular death or hospitalization for worsening heart failure during randomized trial follow-up.
candidate.target_window: Entire randomized trial follow-up, analyzed as time to first event; not a fixed-duration event risk (median follow-up 16 months).

comparison_groups.assignment: Empagliflozin 10 mg once daily added to recommended/usual heart-failure therapy
Placebo added to recommended/usual heart-failure therapy

candidate.reported_outcome: Composite of time to first event of adjudicated cardiovascular death or adjudicated hospitalization for heart failure
candidate.analysis_population: All 3730 randomized patients, analyzed by intention-to-treat using all data obtained through the end of the planned treatment period; 1863 assigned empagliflozin and 1867 placebo. 42 patients were lost to follow-up at varying times (20 placebo, 22 empagliflozin), including 21 with unknown vital status at trial end.

selections.scope_rationale: The selected result directly matches the requested primary composite (cardiovascular death or hospitalization for heart failure), adjudicated and analyzed as time to first event. The requested trial-follow-up window is the reported time-to-event estimand rather than an event risk at a fixed duration; the report gives median follow-up of 16 months. The assignment comparison and hazard-ratio measure also match: empagliflozin 10 mg daily versus placebo, on usual/recommended therapy, HR 0.75 (95% CI 0.65 to 0.86). It is narrower than an unrestricted target population of all randomized patients with reduced-EF heart failure: this trial enrolled only NYHA II-IV patients with LVEF ≤40%, and further enriched eligibility for risk of serious HF events, including criteria for patients with LVEF >30%. The estimate therefore pertains to this qualifying enrolled population, not every possible reduced-EF HF population.
selections.population_rationale: The estimate uses the randomized population under the intention-to-treat principle, rather than an observed-outcome-only subset. Eligibility nevertheless restricted entry to adults with NYHA class II-IV heart failure and LVEF ≤40%, with additional risk criteria for some patients; this is a narrower enrolled population than all patients with reduced-EF heart failure. Some follow-up was incomplete: 42 patients were lost at varying times and 21 had unknown vital status at trial end. These are follow-up limitations, not reported post-randomization eligibility exclusions.
unknowns: The target’s general reduced-EF heart-failure population is broader than this trial’s specified eligibility; effect transport beyond the enrolled risk-enriched population is not established.

Forty-two patients were lost to follow-up, and 21 had unknown vital status at trial end; the primary report notes sensitivity analyses addressing incomplete follow-up, so some event status remains uncertain.

counterevidence.implication: Protocol definition confirms that the endpoint is the adjudicated time-to-first composite, supporting the outcome and time-to-event correspondence rather than a fixed-time risk.
The report documents 42 patients lost to follow-up and 21 with unknown vital status at trial end; this qualifies completeness of follow-up, although the primary analysis remained intention-to-treat.
